findings.summary: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly is a Restricted Gmail scope. Public production needs restricted-scope verification; CASA if restricted data is stored on servers or transmitted. Personal-use and Testing exceptions still impose a user cap and limited refresh-token lifetime. No registered Google application exists on this revision.

Google installed-app OAuth does not support incremental authorization. Calendar must not add calendar scopes onto a Gmail grant or revive the Wave 1 combined connector. Separate consent is two authorizations, two opaque states, two source keys, two connect grants.

calendar.events.readonly views events on all calendars at Google. Kizuki stores one canonical calendar. Narrower calendar.events.owned.readonly is a Calendar-owned decision and must not alter shared auth.

Expired Gmail startHistoryId returns HTTP 404 and requires full resync. Provider does not audit deletions across the gap. Kizuki sets gap and never infers tombstones from absence or GET 404. Snapshot fingerprint mismatch is snapshot_gap_unresolved with no cursor advance.
close/revoke stop the local instance and drain custody. They do not call Google revoke. A completed Google consent followed by refused local enrollment cannot be undone here.
Account identity is OIDC sub. Email, headers, attendees, and message bodies are evidence, not owner or grant authority. Duplicate sub refuses even if disconnected or revoked.
